Vitamin A Deficiency.title: Vitamin A & Beta-Carotene Optimization
regular_foods: Carrots (steamed or cooked in healthy oils)
Sweet potatoes (baked or boiled)
Spinach and fenugreek leaves (palak / methi)
Egg yolks and boiled eggs
Full-fat dairy, yogurt, and paneer
Pumpkin and butternut squash curries or soups
Red and yellow bell peppers
Moringa / drumstick leaves
habits_to_improve: Always consume fat-soluble carotenoids with healthy fats (ghee, olive oil, seeds) to boost absorption by up to 300%
Lightly steam or saute carrots and greens rather than eating purely raw to soften cell walls and release beta-carotene
Avoid boiling vegetables in excessive water where nutrients are discarded; consume cooking broths
Include a colorful orange or dark green vegetable with lunch and dinner daily
what_to_eat: Pair spinach or pumpkin with a teaspoon of extra virgin olive oil or ghee
Eat carrots with hummus, yogurt dip, or roasted nuts
Cook sweet potato wedges with avocado oil and herbs
Incorporate liver or fatty fish (salmon, mackerel) once or twice weekly if non-vegetarian
what_to_avoid: Excessive alcohol intake which depletes hepatic retinol reserves
Strict ultra-low-fat diets which prevent absorption of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, K
Prolonged overcooking of greens in open pans which oxidizes provitamin A
Relying solely on refined carbohydrates without vegetable garnishing

Vitamin B12 Deficiency.title: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin) Replenishment
regular_foods: Eggs (especially whole pasture-raised eggs)
Plain whole-milk yogurt, curd, and kefir
Paneer, cottage cheese, and Swiss cheese
Fortified plant milks (soy, almond, oat milk with added B12)
Fortified whole grain breakfast cereals
Nutritional yeast flakes sprinkled on food
Fish (salmon, tuna, sardines) and poultry
Lean cuts of meat and bone broth
fruits_to_consume: Bananas (rich in vitamin B6 to support cobalamin co-enzyme activity)
Apples and berries (rich in pectin to support healthy gut microbiota)
Oranges and kiwis (vitamin C to support cellular iron and folate balance)
habits_to_improve: Strict vegetarians and vegans must routinely consume fortified nutritional yeast or fortified plant milk
Support stomach acid (avoid excessive antacids/PPIs unless prescribed, as intrinsic factor requires gastric acid)
Eat fermented dairy like kefir or curd between meals to enhance mucosal gut flora
Distribute B12 sources across morning and afternoon meals rather than one large dose
what_to_eat: Scrambled eggs with cheese and whole wheat sourdough toast
Greek yogurt or curd bowl with berries and seeds
Curried paneer with brown rice or chapati
Nutritional yeast stirred into dal, pasta, or roasted vegetables
what_to_avoid: Excessive chronic alcohol consumption which impairs ileal B12 uptake
High intake of raw tea or coffee immediately following a meal containing dairy or eggs
Smoking, which increases cyanide metabolites that deplete active methylcobalamin
Prolonged unmonitored use of acid suppressants (consult doctor if reflux is frequent)

Vitamin C Deficiency.title: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) & Collagen Synthesis
regular_foods: Bell peppers (especially raw yellow and red capsicum)
Broccoli (lightly steamed)
Brussels sprouts and cabbage salads
Tomatoes and fresh tomato rasam/soup
Green chillies and coriander leaves
Cauliflower florets
Spinach and leafy mustard greens
fruits_to_consume: Indian gooseberry (Amla) - extremely high natural ascorbic acid
Guavas (contains up to 4x the vitamin C of an orange)
habits_to_improve: Add fresh lemon juice to warm dal, soups, and curries AFTER turning off the flame (heat destroys vitamin C)
Eat fruit whole and fresh rather than stored juices which lose ascorbic acid through air oxidation
Pair vitamin C rich foods with plant-based iron (lentils, beans) to boost iron absorption by 200%
Keep raw cut vegetable sticks (capsicum, cucumber) ready as everyday mid-morning snacks
what_to_eat: Amla juice or amla murabba in the morning
Fresh citrus salad with guava, pomegranate, and lime zest
Sprouted moong beans tossed with chopped tomatoes, coriander, and fresh lemon
Lightly steamed broccoli with olive oil and garlic
what_to_avoid: Boiling fruits and vegetables for extended periods
Storing cut fruits exposed to air for more than 30 minutes
High intake of processed, deep-fried snacks devoid of antioxidant vitamins
Excessive consumption of sodium-rich canned foods without fresh produce

Vitamin D Deficiency.title: Vitamin D & Calcium Homeostasis
regular_foods: Egg yolks from pasture-raised hens
Fortified milk, fortified curd, and fortified cheeses
Fatty fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines, tuna)
Mushrooms exposed to UV sunlight (e.g. UV-treated portobello or button mushrooms)
Fortified soy milk and almond milk
Fortified orange juices
fruits_to_consume: Fortified orange juice with added vitamin D and calcium
Figs (fresh or dried, high in calcium synergist)
Blackberries and raspberries (magnesium cofactors for vitamin D activation)
habits_to_improve: Spend 15 to 25 minutes in mid-morning sunlight (between 10 AM and 2 PM) with arms and legs exposed
Ensure adequate magnesium and zinc intake (seeds, nuts) required for enzymatic activation of vitamin D
Maintain active weight-bearing physical movement (walking, stairs) to stimulate osteoblast activity
Pair vitamin D rich meals with dietary fats to ensure micellar absorption
what_to_eat: Omelette made with whole eggs, spinach, and mushrooms
Grilled or baked salmon/mackerel with steamed greens
Warm fortified milk with a pinch of turmeric and crushed almonds
UV-treated mushrooms stir-fried with sesame seeds
what_to_avoid: Sedentary indoor lifestyle with zero sunlight exposure
Excessive sunscreen during initial short mid-morning safe sun exposure windows
High consumption of carbonated sodas which leach bone minerals
Crash dieting that eliminates healthy fats necessary for steroid hormone synthesis

Folate (Vitamin B9) Deficiency.title: Folate (B9) Cellular Regeneration
regular_foods: Lentils, chickpeas, kidney beans (rajma), and black beans
Spinach, fenugreek, kale, and collard greens
Asparagus and green peas
Beetroots and beetroot greens
Fortified whole wheat rotis, oats, and barley
Peanuts, sunflower seeds, and flaxseeds
Avocados and edamame
habits_to_improve: Sprout whole lentils (moong, chana) at home; sprouting multiplies bioavailable folate content
Lightly steam greens rather than deep boiling to protect heat-sensitive methylfolates
Eat a bowl of lentil dal or legume soup with every main meal
Snack on raw roasted sunflower seeds or walnuts in the afternoon
what_to_eat: Sprouted moong salad with diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and lime
Steamed asparagus or green peas tossed with olive oil
Chickpea (chole) or rajma curry served with brown rice
Avocado mash on multi-seed toast
what_to_avoid: Excessive alcohol intake which directly hinders intestinal folate absorption
Overcooking beans until dissolved without using the bean broth
Relying entirely on white bleached flour (maida) products lacking fortification
Smoking and high chronic mental stress without adequate dietary replenishments

Iron Deficiency & Anemia.title: Iron & Hemoglobin Building Nutrition
regular_foods: Lentils, red beans, chickpeas, and black grams
Spinach, moringa / drumstick leaves, and beet greens
Tofu and fermented tempeh
Pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds (til), and chia seeds
Jaggery (gur) used as an occasional sweetener with roasted grams
Lean meats, liver, and eggs (heme iron with high bioavailability)
Dates, dried figs (anjeer), and black raisins
fruits_to_consume: Guavas (high vitamin C to maximize non-heme iron absorption)
habits_to_improve: NEVER drink chai, tea, or coffee within 60 minutes of lunch or dinner (tannins block up to 70% of iron)
Cook curries, gravies, and tomato rasam in traditional cast iron pans to naturally enrich food with dietary iron
Always pair plant-based iron foods with a source of vitamin C (lemon squeeze, amla, tomato)
Soak beans, lentils, and seeds for 4 to 8 hours before cooking to degrade phytates
what_to_eat: Cast iron cooked dal with squeezed fresh lemon juice
Handful of roasted chana with dates or a small cube of jaggery
Moringa leaf stir fry with grated coconut
Soaked black raisins and dried figs first thing in the morning
what_to_avoid: Drinking black tea, green tea, or milk tea right after main meals
Consuming high-calcium supplements or antacids simultaneously with iron-rich foods
Unsoaked whole grains and raw wheat bran containing high phytic acid
Processed ultra-refined snacks that displace wholesome nutrient-dense meals

General / Multiple Micronutrient Support.title: Holistic Micronutrient & Vitality Protocol
regular_foods: Rainbow vegetable medley (greens, orange carrots, red tomatoes, purple cabbage)
Sprouted whole grains and whole pulses (moong, horsegram, chickpeas)
Cultured yogurts, homemade buttermilk (chaas), and kefir
Mixed raw nuts (almonds, walnuts) and seeds (pumpkin, sunflower, flax)
Cold-pressed oils (extra virgin olive oil, cold-pressed sesame or mustard oil)
Clean lean proteins and eggs
fruits_to_consume: Bananas and papayas for prebiotic gut support
Apples with peel intact for quercetin and fiber
Fresh coconut water for natural electrolyte balance
habits_to_improve: Aim for at least 30 different plant foods per week (grains, legumes, veggies, nuts, seeds, fruits)
Chew food thoroughly to facilitate digestive enzyme release and optimal nutrient breakdown
Hydrate with 2.5 to 3 liters of pure water daily away from large heavy meals
Establish a consistent 7-8 hour sleep schedule to allow cellular repair and nutrient utilization
what_to_eat: Colorful grain bowl with quinoa/brown rice, roasted vegetables, and tahini dressing
Sprout and pomegranate chaat with fresh herbs and lemon juice
Homemade vegetable soup cooked in iron or earthenware with mixed seeds
Golden turmeric milk with black pepper and crushed almond flakes
what_to_avoid: Ultra-processed packaged foods high in trans-fats, refined corn syrup, and preservatives
Skipping meals followed by late-night bingeing on fast foods
Chronic sleep deprivation which disrupts gut nutrient absorption and increases cortisol
Sedentary posture for consecutive hours without light stretching breaks
